assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks beat the earlier single-ion and microwave standards in stability by using many atoms interrogated at the magic wavelength, and they have redefined what can be measured: fractional uncertainties near 1e-18, relativistic geodesy at the centimetre scale, and tests of fundamental constants. Clear, original, instrument-defining physics, squarely in the tradition of measurement advances that open new science.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and first demonstrated the Sr lattice clock; Ye led the realization of the highest-accuracy and stability clocks and the many-body and JILA-style systematic-control work. The two-person credit is clean. Others (Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow, Hinkley) are not in the credited list, so a two-person prize is the fair configuration here.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of independent confirmation across several groups and species (Sr, Yb, Hg); clock comparisons and a pending redefinition of the SI second make this timely, not premature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wishes to pair this with the earlier frequency-comb and ion-clock recognition (2005, 2012) or sees it as incremental over them.
Credit among the early lattice-clock proposers is not fully resolved by the supplied text; I rely on my recollection of the history.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal showed how cold trapped ions could be used as a scalable quantum register with gates mediated by shared motion, and experiments realized entangling gates, algorithms and error-corrected operations at high fidelity. The idea is foundational to a platform that is now among the leading approaches to quantum computing.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller provided the decisive theory; Blatt's group gave the first gate realization of the Cirac-Zoller scheme and key subsequent demonstrations. Wineland and Monroe are not in the credited list (Wineland already has a 2012 prize), so Cirac-Zoller-Blatt is a coherent theory-plus-experiment trio. B001 and B005 overlap, so the exact scope of the citation needs care.
assessment.maturity: Mature: nearly three decades of experimental follow-through with multiple independent laboratories and now commercial machines. Recognition is timely, with the recent 2025 superconducting-circuit prize not displacing the ion platform.
uncertainties: Overlap with Wineland's 2012 prize and with the Cirac/Zoller optical-lattice and Rydberg candidates may complicate the citation.
Whether Blatt or other ion-trap experimentalists (Monroe, Wineland group) have the stronger claim to the experimental half.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Matter-wave interferometry with atoms is a core precision-measurement tool, used for gravimetry, gradiometry, tests of the equivalence principle and measurements of the fine-structure constant and G. It is conceptually elegant and has a real record of making new quantities measurable.
assessment.attribution: Bordé's theory of atom interferometry with light-pulse beam splitters, Pritchard's first demonstrations with nanofabricated gratings and the Mach-Zehnder-type atom interferometers, and Kasevich and Chu's light-pulse gravimeters all contributed. Steven Chu and others are not in the credited list, so the allocation is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Well established and independently confirmed, with applications now maturing into field instruments; the major physics results (e.g. large-scale tests) are still developing, so the prize would reward method more than a headline discovery.
uncertainties: Credit is distributed among more people than the list covers, including Chu, Chu-Kasevich and Pritchard's group.
Impact so far is more as an instrument than as a transformative discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection and coherent control of single nitrogen-vacancy centres in diamond opened solid-state quantum sensing at room temperature, with nanoscale magnetometry, thermometry and biological sensing and spin-based quantum registers. This is a vivid example of quantum control used as a measurement tool.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup and Jelezko demonstrated single-NV optical detection and coherent control; Lukin contributed to quantum registers, sensing proposals and applications. Allocation is plausible, though other groups (Awschalom, Hanson, Budker) have strong claims.
assessment.maturity: Broad independent confirmation and a large worldwide community; applications are growing and the field is mature enough, although the strongest sensing applications are still emerging.
uncertainties: Attribution relative to Hanson, Awschalom and other NV pioneers is contested.
Practical impact in sensing is promising but is less settled than in precision time-keeping.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution links quantum foundations to security: the BB84 protocol and the Ekert entanglement-based scheme underlie experimental quantum cryptography and quantum networks. The concept is original and has led to both laboratory and satellite demonstrations.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard proposed BB84; Ekert proposed the entanglement-based E91 protocol. The three credited names give a natural configuration, though Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea is a known historical point.
assessment.maturity: The concepts are decades old and experimentally verified in many labs, but the practical security and deployment of QKD are still debated, and the 2022 prize for entanglement experiments already covers part of the territory.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 Bell-test prize and with the Nobel interest in quantum foundations.
Practical-security debate and lack of a decisive discovery moment may reduce the case.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rydberg blockade with optical tweezers has made programmable neutral-atom arrays a leading platform for quantum simulation and emerging quantum computing, with hundreds of qubits and results on many-body dynamics. Exciting physics, drawing on laser cooling and single-atom control.
assessment.attribution: The credited list contains four names; a prize can have at most three, and the selection must come from Browaeys, Saffman, Lukin and Zoller. I would propose Lukin, Saffman and Zoller as the strongest theory-plus-experiment combination, but Browaeys and others (Greiner, Ahn, Bernien) also have claims.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly moving; many key results are from the last decade and still developing. Timing suggests this may be premature relative to the settled topics above.
uncertainties: Premature relative to more established topics.
Allocation of credit among four names and unlisted researchers is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cooling, trapping and controlling molecules at ultracold temperatures supports precision tests of fundamental physics (e.g. electron EDM), ultracold chemistry and quantum simulation with dipolar interactions. The experimental difficulty is real and the work is conceptually important.
assessment.attribution: DeMille, Doyle and Ye are central in different aspects: laser cooling and buffer-gas cooling of molecules and precision measurement with them. Ni, Jin and the Ye group contributed to ultracold KRb as well, and Debbie Jin is deceased, which complicates a fair configuration.
assessment.maturity: Active and still maturing; key demonstrations of direct laser cooling and EDM improvements are recent, with a wider impact still being established.
uncertainties: A coherent single discovery is not obvious; the topic combines several techniques.
Credit allocation is unsettled given Jin's death and other major contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cavity optomechanics and quantum acoustics demonstrate ground-state cooling, squeezed and entangled mechanical states and quantum control of macroscopic oscillators, with gravitational-wave detection and sensing applications. This is conceptually interesting and experimentally strong.
assessment.attribution: Kippenberg and Aspelmeyer contributed foundational experiments and reviews; Cleland contributed the quantum acoustics demonstrations with superconducting qubits. Other significant contributors (Harris, Painter, Lehnert, Schwab) are not in the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Established for about 15 years but with application impact still developing, and the 2025 Nobel for macroscopic quantum effects in circuits overlaps in spirit.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum phenomena.
Unclear which individual discovery would be cited.
